name: send_email
description: Send an email. Required: `to` + `body`; `subject` is optional. Can also reach a phone via the SMS-via-email gateway. To attach files, pass `pod_ids` (see that field). Do not use email to talk to the user directly unless explicitly instructed.

inputs.name: pod_ids
inputs.description: Optional list of pod URIs to attach as files. Pass each pod_id EXACTLY as returned by pod_search or mint_pod_from_path — including the `datapod:<kind>:` prefix. Lookup is exact-match. File-backed pods (image / video / audio / document) attach as their stored file with original filename and inferred MIME type. Body-only pods (email / chat_cluster / text / transcript / note) are rendered to a tempfile (.eml for email pods, .txt for the rest) and attached — the agent never reads the body, the render happens at tool execution time. This is the courier path: pass the pod_id, never pod_fetch the body, and the recipient gets the content as an attachment.

inputs.name: inline_pod_ids
inputs.description: Optional list of pod URIs to PASTE INLINE into the email body (instead of attaching as a file). For each pod the tool fetches the body and appends a delimited block to `body` — for email pods that's the standard `----- Forwarded message -----` block with From / Subject / Date headers; for other body-only kinds it's a `---` separator + one-liner + body. The agent never reads the body — fetch happens at tool execution, same privacy story as `pod_ids`. Use `inline_pod_ids` when the recipient should see the content directly in the email body (typical for forwarding emails or pasting a transcript); use `pod_ids` when they should get an attachment to download. Both are valid courier paths and should be preferred over pod_fetch + handcrafted body.

arguments_prompt:
Arguments for sending an email:
to: str
subject: Optional[str]
body: Optional[str]
pod_ids: Optional[List[str]]  # Pod URIs to ATTACH as files (file-backed pods → stored file; body-only pods → rendered .eml/.txt). Tool reads body, agent doesn't.
inline_pod_ids: Optional[List[str]]  # Pod URIs to PASTE INLINE into the email body — email pods get a Gmail-style `----- Forwarded message -----` block; other kinds get a `---` separator. Tool reads body, agent doesn't. Pick pod_ids for attachments, inline_pod_ids for inline forwarding. Don't pod_fetch then handcraft `body` unless you actually need to edit/summarize the content.

metadata.planner_description: Send an email (or SMS via email gateway).
